title: Algebraic structure in holographic tensor networks
abstract: Tests the proposal (2511.21852) that generalized entanglement wedges carry subalgebras of observables, using holographic tensor networks. A generalized-entanglement-wedge analogue is a region with no containing region of fewer boundary legs. In the large-bond-dimension limit each such region has a canonical boundary subalgebra; intersections, joins and commutants are related to geometric operations on network regions; an algebraic entropy obeys monotonicity and SSA; a type II_1 algebra is built from a sequence of random tensor networks with growing bond dimension (ultraproduct).
key_claims: In isometric / large-D random tensor networks, extremal regions (minimal boundary-leg count) have canonically associated boundary subalgebras
Algebraic operations on these subalgebras track geometric operations on network regions; non-isometric maps 'proceed through a minimal cut'
Analysis ASSUMES exact isometry of extremal-region maps; approximate isometries at finite D are explicitly set aside
No MERA, no optimized (energy-minimized) network, no numerics
relevance_note: Full text grep-read. This is the formal statement of the 'cut-like' picture in the idealized regime (exact isometries, D -> infinity). HYP-033 (SIM-2026-079, outcome 4) found that an optimized chi=6 MERA is NOT cut-like and is indistinguishable from Haar at that chi, a finite-chi, optimized-network regime this paper explicitly excludes. So it neither pre-empts nor contradicts HYP-033; it is the idealized baseline that HYP-033's 'cut' outcome represented. Must-cite for any HYP-033 write-up and for a philosophy-of-physics piece on state functionals vs network-sensitive observables (a network-region -> algebra map is a network-sensitive object, but it is only established where the network is ideal). v1 2026-09-30, v2 2026-10-02.
